content.text: I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the file list and the usual layout of this boilerplate. The line numbers are estimates and none of this has been checked against the code.

candidates.explanation: On a password change, AuthService.update ends the user's other sessions by calling sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude. The exclude id is probably wrong here. It is likely the user id or another wrong field, not the current session id (userJwtPayload.sessionId). The current session then gets deleted, so its next refresh returns 401. An unrelated session whose id happens to match the wrong value survives, which would explain why an older session on another device 'sometimes' survives.

The exclusion filter may be wrong. It may filter on the wrong column, such as user.id compared with excludeId. It may also compare mismatched types, for example a number against a string, or use Not() incorrectly. Either way the current session is deleted and another one is kept.
This is the same defect for the MongoDB backend. The $ne filter or the id conversion on the excluded session id may be wrong. The current session is then not excluded from deletion.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: user.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }) after the password change. Make sure the session repositories exclude that session id with the right field and type: Not(excludeId) in TypeORM, or $ne with the matching id type in Mongoose. They should delete every other session for that user.
